key_insight: 3D opto-electro-thermal simulations show that lead-free MgXS3 (X = Ti, Zr, Hf) chalcogenide perovskites can enable high-efficiency solar cells when absorber thickness, doping, defect density, and an Sb2S3 BSF are jointly optimized.
engineering_relevance: The study provides device-design guidance for building thermally stable, non-toxic, high-performance perovskite-inspired solar cells in realistic 3D geometries.
method: 3D finite-element COMSOL simulation of a ZnSe/MgXS3/Sb2S3 solar-cell stack
Self-consistent coupling of optical generation, drift-diffusion transport, and heat transfer under AM 1.5G illumination
Parameter sweeps on absorber thickness, doping, defect density, and BSF contribution
evidence_signal: Optimized simulated performance reached 28.18% PCE for MgZrS3, 26.72% for MgTiS3, and 28.16% for MgHfS3, with corresponding VOC, JSC, and FF values reported in the abstract.
watch_item: Results are simulation-based and depend on material parameters and interface assumptions, so experimental validation and fabrication tolerance remain important concerns.
paper_title: Numerical exploration on unveiling the photovoltaic potential of MgXS3(X = Ti, Zr, Hf) chalcogenide perovskites
